description: From a change-data-capture (CDC) log of customer updates, produce the current state of each customer. For each customer_id keep only the most recent change by updated_at (ties broken by higher change_seq). If the most recent change has op = 'D' (delete), the customer must not appear in the output. Output columns: customer_id (INT64), email (STRING), tier (STRING), updated_at (TIMESTAMP).

change_seq.description: Monotonic sequence number assigned by the CDC connector

email.description: Email after the change; NULL on delete records

tier.description: Loyalty tier after the change; NULL on delete records

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the change in the source system

loaded_at.description: When the batch landed in BigQuery

edge_cases: Customer whose latest operation is a delete must be excluded
Two changes with the same updated_at are ordered by change_seq
Customer deleted and later re-inserted must appear with the re-inserted values
common_failure_modes: FM3: Filtering op != 'D' before picking the latest row resurrects deleted customers with their pre-delete values
FM7: No deterministic tie-breaker in ORDER BY makes the result non-reproducible when updated_at collides
